## Installation

Install the quarto extension:

```sh
quarto add quarto-graph
```

Then install the Python package, which resolves the graph data:

```sh
uv add quarto-graph
```

## Add to `_quarto.yml`

Set the project type to `quarto-graph` and add it to `filters`:

```yaml
project:
  type: quarto-graph

filters:
  - quarto-graph
```

## Using wikilinks

Type `[[Home]]` to link to a page named "Home", without knowing its file path.

Give a page an alias with the `also-known-as` frontmatter key. For example, in
`/index.qmd`:

```markdown
---
title: quarto-graph
also-known-as: Home
---
```

Then link to it from any other page:

*some-other-page/index.qmd*:

```markdown
Go back to [[Home]] using this wikilink
```

Regular markdown links work the same way. These are equivalent:

- `[[Home]]`
- `[Home](index.qmd)`

See [[Wikilinks and Aliases]] for the full linking syntax.

### Display text and anchors

Add `|` to show custom link text instead of the target's title:

`[[Home|back home]]`

Link to a heading with `#`:

`[[Home#Installation]]`

Combine both:

`[[Home#Installation|see install steps]]`

## Graphs in your website

Once pages are connected, embed a graph and get backlinks automatically.

Insert the graph widget as a shortcode:

`{{{< quarto-graph-full >}}}`

{{< quarto-graph-full >}}

Any page with incoming wikilinks or markdown links gets a "Backlinks" section
appended automatically. No shortcode needed.

See [[The Graph Widget]] for more about the graph widget, how to embed it in
pages, and how to customize it.

## Render

The approach this extension takes is to resolve links at render time. Nothing
rewrites your `.qmd` source files.

## Frontmatter reference

| Key | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `title:` | Page title, and the link text shown when a wikilink has no `\|display` override |
| `type:` | Colors the node in the graph widget: `concept`, `person`, `reference`, `project`, `experiment`, `moc`; anything else (or omitted) falls back to gray |
| `also-known-as:` | Extra names this page's wikilinks can be reached by, on top of its filename. A separate key from Quarto's own `aliases:`; see [[Wikilinks and Aliases]] for why |
| `quarto-graph:` | Per-page override of the sidebar mini-panel (`sidebar: true/false`, or `sidebar: {enabled, depth}`); see [[The Graph Widget]] |
